parts.title: My first marathon
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Two years ago, I could not run for ten minutes without stopping. My friend Ana laughed when I told her that I wanted to run a marathon, but then she promised to train with me. We started with short runs, three times a week, and slowly we added distance.

The training was harder than I had imagined. In January, it was dark and freezing in the mornings, and I often wanted to stay in bed. What kept me going was the group. Every Sunday, twenty of us met in the park for a long run, and afterwards, we all had breakfast together.

On the day of the marathon, I was so nervous that I could not eat. The start was exciting, with thousands of people and music on every corner. For the first twenty kilometres, I felt wonderful. Then my legs began to hurt, and the last part was a real struggle. Ana stayed next to me and kept talking about silly things to make me laugh.

I finished in five hours and ten minutes. It was not fast, but I cried with happiness at the finish line. Next year, I plan to do it again and to beat my time.

questions.explanation: Ana laughed when the writer told her about the marathon.

questions.explanation: She says that what kept her going was the group.

questions.prompt: How did she feel on the day of the race?
questions.explanation: She was so nervous that she could not eat.

questions.prompt: What did Ana do in the last part of the race?
questions.explanation: Ana stayed next to her and talked about silly things to make her laugh.

questions.prompt: What does the writer plan to do next year?
questions.explanation: She plans to do it again and to beat her time.

parts.title: How to prepare for a race
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Preparing for a race starts weeks before the big day. [1] Beginners should run three times a week, with rest days in between, so that their legs can recover.

Food is also important. [2] Many runners eat pasta the night before, because it gives them energy for the next day.

On the morning of the race, you should get up early. [3] This gives your body time to digest breakfast, and it stops you from rushing.

During the race, do not start too fast. [4] Many people run the first kilometres too quickly, and then they have no energy left at the end.

After the race, you should walk slowly for a few minutes. [5] Then drink plenty of water and eat something light, and your body will recover much faster.
sentences: Good shoes are more important than expensive clothes.
Save your energy for the second half of the race.
Increase the distance slowly, week by week.
Cold weather is the best time to run fast.
Aim to finish eating at least two hours before the start.
What you eat in the last days can make a big difference.
Stopping suddenly can make your muscles stiff.
Running shoes are becoming more colourful every year.

gaps.explanation: Training starts weeks before; the next sentence says how often beginners should run.
Food is important, and the next sentence gives pasta as an example.
You should get up early to finish eating two hours before; the next sentence says this gives time to digest.
Do not start too fast and save energy; the next sentence says many people run too quickly.
Walking slowly after the race is because stopping suddenly makes muscles stiff.

parts.passage: Hi Linden, guess what? I have signed up [1] a ten-kilometre race next month! I started running three months ago, and I have already [2] five kilometres without stopping. My coach says that I am improving more quickly [3] most beginners. I run every morning [4] seven, before breakfast. It is not always easy, especially when it rains, but I never miss a session. There is a club for beginners in the park, [5] you can join us any time. Do you remember the old days [6] we used to run round the school field? Colt

questions.prompt: Gap 3

parts.title: Why running is so popular
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Running is one of the most popular sports in the world. You do not need much equipment, [1] a good pair of shoes. You can run almost anywhere, at any time of the day, and it is usually free. [2] you run with a friend, the time passes more quickly. After a hard day at work or school, a short run can clear your head [3] make you feel much better. Of course, it is important not to do too much [4] once. Beginners often start too fast and then hurt themselves. It is better to run slowly [5] first and to increase the distance gradually. Anybody can do it, [6] matter how old or how fit they are.

gaps.explanation: Except means apart from: you need only a good pair of shoes.
If you run with a friend, the time passes more quickly.
And joins the two results: clear your head and make you feel better.
At once is a fixed phrase meaning at the same time.
At first is a fixed phrase meaning in the beginning.
No matter how is a fixed phrase.

parts.title: A meeting for marathon volunteers
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: organiser
turns.text: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming to this meeting for volunteers. My name is Gower, and I’m the organiser. First, the date. Last year the marathon was on the first Sunday of April, but that was Easter weekend and many people were away, so this year it takes place on the second Sunday of April. The charity dinner is the night before, on Saturday, and you’re all invited. We expect a lot of runners. Two years ago we had four thousand, and last year five thousand, but this time about six thousand people have signed up, so we need all of you. Now, the timetable. The first runners will start at nine o’clock, not at eight as in the past, because the city council wants the roads to be closed for a shorter time. Volunteers should arrive at seven, so that we have time to prepare. You will all receive a T-shirt. The runners wear white and the staff of the city wear green, so we chose a different colour for you: yellow. That way everybody can see you from far away. Please wear dark trousers with it. On the route there are water stations. In the old plan there were ten, but it will be hot this year, so we’ve added two more, which makes twelve altogether. Each station needs eight volunteers, and I’ll give you the map at the end. One more thing: you’ll be standing for a long time, so wear comfortable shoes. Finally, a thank you. After the race, in the main square, there will be free food for all volunteers. Some of you asked for sandwiches, and the café on the corner offered cakes, but in the end the best price was from the pizza restaurant by the river, so you’ll get a slice and a drink. Thank you, and see you in April.

gaps.prompt: The marathon takes place on the second ___ of April
gaps.explanation: He says it takes place on the second Sunday of April; Saturday is the charity dinner.
Four and five thousand were earlier years; this time about six thousand have signed up.
It starts at nine, not at eight as in the past; volunteers arrive at seven.
Runners wear white and city staff wear green, so the volunteers’ colour is yellow.

gaps.prompt: There are ___ water stations along the route
gaps.explanation: There were ten in the old plan and they added two more, which makes twelve.

gaps.prompt: After the race, there will be free ___
gaps.explanation: Sandwiches and cakes were offered, but the volunteers will get pizza and a drink.

parts.title: An interview with a desert runner
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Pardo, you ran a race of two hundred and fifty kilometres in the desert. Why did you enter it?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Everybody asks me that. I’d like to say the prize money, because the winner gets a lot, but honestly, I never expected to win. I’m an amateur and a teacher. I wasn’t looking for new friends either, I have plenty. I read an article about this race years ago, and one question kept coming back: could I do it? I needed to know what my body and my head could really do.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Where did you sleep during the race?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: That surprised people. I thought we would have a small hotel at the end of each day, and I even looked for one in the first village, but they were full of tourists. Some of the support staff slept in their cars, but the runners could not. The organisers put us in tents. Ten of us shared one, and the noise was incredible, because everybody snored.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What was the hardest part?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Many people think it’s the cold at night, and yes, the temperature fell to almost zero, but a good sleeping bag solved that. Loneliness wasn’t a problem either. On the long stretches there is silence, and I enjoyed it. The real enemy was the sun, forty-five degrees at noon, and my feet. By the second day I had eleven blisters and I could hardly put on my shoes.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What helped you on the third day?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Honestly, I wanted to quit that morning. A day of rest wasn’t allowed, because the race doesn’t stop, and a big breakfast only made me feel sick. Then an older woman from Canada ran beside me for an hour. Her advice was simple. She told me how to look after my feet and to divide the distance into small parts. After that I felt like a different person.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: So what did you learn?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I don’t believe people who say that races like this are quite easy, because nothing about it was easy. Prizes don’t matter either, the winner had a big cheque and looked sad. What I learned is that if you take one small step and then another, you can go very far. It works for life as well as for running.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: And what’s next for you?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: People think I’ll stop, and my wife would love that, but no. Another desert? Maybe later, the sand finished me. Next year I’m going to run in the mountains, in Peru, for ten days. It will be cold and the air is thin, so it will be a different kind of test.

questions.prompt: Why did Pardo enter the race?
questions.explanation: He says he never expected the prize, he has plenty of friends, and he wanted to know what his body and head could do.

questions.prompt: Where did the runners sleep?
questions.explanation: The hotels were full and only the staff had cars; the organisers gave each group a tent.

questions.prompt: What was the hardest part for him?
questions.explanation: The cold was solved by a sleeping bag and he liked the silence; the sun and the blisters were the problem.

questions.prompt: Why did Pardo feel better on the third day?
questions.explanation: A day of rest was not allowed and the breakfast made him sick; a Canadian woman told him what to do.

questions.prompt: What did he learn?
questions.explanation: He says races are not easy and prizes do not matter; what he learned is that small steps take you far.

questions.explanation: He will not stop and not go to another desert yet; next year he will run in the mountains in Peru.
